title: Private VPC deployment: operational contract, airgap validation matrix and offline image provisioning PRD
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Purpose: define the operational contract and acceptance criteria for Private (VPC/on-prem) Redwood deployments with explicit requirements for air-gapped/offline upgrade flows, minimal egress assumptions, image and artifact provisioning, and runbook/validation matrices used by Solutions and SRE during customer onboarding and upgrades. This PRD focuses on networking constraints, artifact delivery options, verification rules, and the tests + observability required to signoff an upgrade in isolated environments.
background: Customer demand for fully air-gapped and highly restricted VPC installs has increased. Previous tickets covered specific upgrade gates and isolated bootstrap contracts, but teams still lack a single, prescriptive operational contract customers can implement and that our install + upgrade automation can validate. This document consolidates modes (online, controlled-egress, offline bundle), required network allowlist targets, signing and verification rules, and the acceptance tests the deployment team will run for final signoff.
scope_included: Network allowlist matrix for three deployment modes: online (no restrictions), controlled-egress (limited outbound), offline/airgapped (no outbound)
Offline upgrade mechanism: signed artifact bundle (tar + metadata), local registry import, image verification and deterministic upgrade order
Operational runbook + checklist for Solutions and SRE to validate and execute an offline upgrade
Acceptance tests for DNS, service discovery, KMS integration, and audit-log continuity post-upgrade
Compatibility with private registries (Harbor, ACR, GCR mirror) and basic auth/service-account flows
scope_excluded: Design of per-customer custom network appliances (we define interfaces not hardware)
Automatic artifact mirroring over custom third-party WAN accelerators (out of scope for MVP)
Edge-device/embedded installs (this focuses on datacenter/VPC k8s installs)
Detailed HSM vendor-specific integration (we specify KMS/HSM contract but not vendor SDKs)
network_requirements: Controlled-Egress mode: allowlist should consist of <control-plane-endpoints>, <package-index-mirrors>, time/CRL check endpoints. Minimal TCP/443 egress to 6 FQDNs must be documented per-region.
Offline/Airgap mode: no outbound connectivity required after initial bundle ingestion. Bootstrapping artifacts must be importable via a local registry or file-install path.
Split-horizon DNS: support explicit FQDN overrides and local DNS entries for internal service discovery; runbook must include validation commands and expected DNS records.
MTU and IP ranges: document recommended MTU >= 1400, and example IP/CIDR constraints for control plane and data plane isolation.
Proxy support: deployments behind HTTP(S) proxies must be supported; image pulls and control-plane callbacks must honor proxy env vars and certificate pinning.
TLS: all control-plane traffic must use TLS; certificate rotation must be possible without requiring external CA access during upgrade
artifact_and_image_requirements: All distributable artifacts (images, charts, manifests) must be published as a signed bundle with an accompanying manifest.json signed with our release key and optionally customer's verification key.
Bundle formats supported: OCI image tarballs + Helm chart tar, and an 'airgap-manifest' JSON that lists image digests and install ordering.
Verification: installer must verify image digests and GPG or cosign signatures before performing any writes to cluster state.
Local registries: we must support import into private registries (Harbor/ACR) and provide scripts to re-tag and push images; documentation for registry auth (basic, robot account) included.
Deterministic upgrade DAG: bundles must include explicit pre/post hooks and migration steps; the installer will validate DAG consistency prior to execution.
offline_upgrade_flow: Produce signed airgap bundle for target release with manifest and signature
Customer or Solutions engineer imports bundle into local storage / local registry
Run 'preflight-airgap' checks which validate cluster capacity, DNS entries, and KMS availability
Installer performs image verification (signature + digest) and stages components in a dry-run mode
Perform canary subset upgrade (configurable % of instances) with automated health probes
If health criteria met, continue to full rollout; otherwise abort and trigger rollback path using preserved manifests
Post-upgrade validation: run acceptance test suite and capture telemetry snapshot for audit
image_signing_and_verification: Primary signing: Redwood release team signs every bundle with cosign + key stored in hardened CI
Customer verification: support optional additional signature by customer's offline signing tooling; installer accepts an allowlist of signing keys
Failure modes: any signature or digest mismatch must fail the upgrade and emit an explicit forensics artifact (bundle id, failing image, expected digest)
Key rotation: runbook for rotating verification keys locally without contacting Redwood control plane
kms_and_secrets_requirements: Support for customer-managed KMS in VPC (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) with offline key negotiation options
For airgapped installs, provide a mechanism to pre-provision encrypted secrets used by the platform; secrets must be importable via sealed secret manifests or KMS-wrapped blobs
Audit logs: all secret unwrap operations during upgrades must be recorded and exportable in an audit bundle
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: The installer can perform a full product upgrade from release A -> release B in an environment with zero outbound access (airgap) using only a signed bundle and local registry import

AC-2: Controlled-egress mode succeeds when only the documented allowlist endpoints are reachable. Tests validate binary downloads, time CRL checks, and adaptive kernel selection without additional endpoints
AC-3: All images and charts are verified by signature and digest before any cluster state change. A mismatch prevents the upgrade and logs a forensics artifact
AC-4: KMS integration works post-upgrade in airgapped and controlled-egress modes; a preflight check verifies key access and permissions
AC-5: Service discovery via split-horizon DNS resolves expected FQDNs after upgrade; automated DNS validation tests pass
AC-6: Runbook steps produce reproducible results when executed by Solutions engineers; we measure time-to-complete and document variance <= 30% for similar cluster sizes

AC-7: Rollback executes deterministically and returns the cluster to the previous healthy state within the documented outage window for the tier (<= 15 minutes for critical control-plane components or documented exception)
AC-8: Observability: upgrade telemetry (component version map, node health, error traces) are captured and exportable as an audit artifact for customer and Redwood SRE review
test_plan: TP-1: Airgap upgrade dry-run: run installer in dry-run against bundle and verify verification step outputs
TP-2: Airgap full upgrade: non-prod cluster with no outbound egress; validate all ACs and record logs
TP-3: Controlled-egress validation: simulate allowlist-only network and verify successful image pulls and CRL checks
TP-4: Negative test: corrupt one image digest in manifest and ensure installer fails gracefully and produces forensics artifact
TP-5: KMS failover: simulate KMS unavailability and validate preflight fails with actionable message
TP-6: DNS split-horizon: update local resolver entries and validate service discovery for control-plane and data-plane components
TP-7: Performance gating: run upgrade on a cluster with constrained resources to confirm installer respects admission limits and aborts with clear remediation steps
monitoring_and_metrics: Upgrade success rate over last 30 days
Median upgrade duration by cluster size
Time between bundle signing and installer acceptance (to catch stale bundles)
rollout_and_rollback_policy: Default rollout: canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with health gating at each stage
Health gating: readiness probe latency, error rate, and control-plane reconciliation time thresholds defined per component
Rollback triggers: failed health gate, repeated pod crash loops for >2x threshold, or any verification failure post-stage
Rollback path: use preserved previous manifests and image digests; rollback must preserve persistent data and reindex where necessary
Operational communication: Solutions/SRE must open a documented upgrade incident with timelines and collect telemetry bundle for postmortem if rollback occurs
runbook_requirements: Pre-upgrade checklist (capacity, backups, KMS access, DNS entries, local registry health)
Step-by-step offline upgrade commands with expected outputs and common remediation steps
Post-upgrade validation and test script outputs to capture (health snapshot, logs, index checks)
Troubleshooting section mapping error messages to remedial actions and links to runbook playbooks
Template incident report for Solutions/SRE with required fields and linked telemetry artifacts
documentation_and_training: Create customer-facing install guide for airgap and controlled-egress flows
Internal Solutions training workshop and checklist signoff template
Example scripts for bundle import and local registry re-tagging
Short video walkthrough for common offline upgrade pitfalls
decisions: Use cosign as primary signing tool for bundles (decided 2026-02-25)
Support 2 artifact import paths: OCI tar import and registry push; prefer registry for large deployments
Adopt deterministic DAG manifest format for upgrade ordering and pre/post hooks
open_questions: Q1: Do we require mandatory customer signature for every release or make it opt-in? (impact on automation and support workload)
Q2: Should we provide a hosted mirror accelerator appliance as a paid add-on for very large customers?
Q3: What is the maximum supported bundle size before we recommend alternate transfer methods (physical media)?
